R387.note: Replaces the powershell.exe shell-out with System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping so serverName is never re-parsed as script; the output is now a hand-formatted approximation of Test-Connection's text rather than the original, which the write-up states, and the added empty-serverName 400 only rejects a value the original could not have pinged.

R388.note: Stored extension now comes from file-type's detected.ext instead of req.file.originalname, so a PNG named .php is stored as .png; response shape and 415 path unchanged.

R389.note: Rejects CR/LF in reply-to, recipient and subject before they reach the SMTP command stream, which closes the CRLF command injection; the only newly rejected values (CRLF-bearing or null addresses) were never legitimate SMTP input.

R390.note: Parameterised with @actor via AddWithValue; apostrophes are now literal data, COUNT(*) cast and the JSON {count} response are unchanged.

R391.note: Random hex name plus file-type's detected extension replaces originalname, closing both traversal and dangerous-extension storage; the returned url now carries the generated name, which the write-up states, and the 400 error shape is intact.

R392.note: app.UseAntiforgery() alone does not validate this endpoint: the antiforgery middleware only checks endpoints carrying IAntiforgeryMetadata with RequiresValidation=true, which minimal APIs add automatically for form-bound parameters only, and this JSON-bound MapPost gets none, so without .RequireAntiforgery() on the endpoint (or a manual IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync) a cross-site POST still reaches QueueAsync; nothing observable changes for legitimate callers.

R393.note: Magic-byte check of the first bytes against the declared type (PNG 89 50 4E 47, JPEG FF D8 FF) before the copy, using a fresh getInputStream() for the write so the copy is not truncated; only content/type mismatches are newly rejected, and the stored name and response are unchanged.

R394.note: Secure: true set on the session cookie; the added HttpOnly is stated hardening that blocks no legitimate use of a session token.

R395.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding().withRootObject(order) removes the TypeLocator, MethodResolver, ConstructorResolver and BeanResolver so T(), method calls, new and @bean are rejected, while property reads and arithmetic on OrderContext still evaluate through the same ReflectivePropertyAccessor the original used.

R396.note: Moves the pending_cart_id session write after login_user() so the cart id is only stored in the authenticated session, matching the reported ordering defect; no other behaviour changes.

R397.note: json_decode does prevent object instantiation, but it changes the cookie's wire format: every cookie the (unchanged, out-of-diff) writer emitted with serialize() now decodes to null and silently yields an empty cart, while the write-up claims functionality is preserved; the format-preserving fix is unserialize($rawCookie, ['allowed_classes' => ['ShoppingCart']]) or false plus field copy.

R398.note: Positional placeholder with '%' . $term . '%' bound through execute(), preserving the substring LIKE semantics while quotes can no longer alter the query structure.

R399.note: Build FAIL (CS0120): RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(byte[]) is an instance method, so the static call does not compile (the static form is RandomNumberGenerator.Fill(bytes) or GetBytes(int)); the intended change of ignoring the seed is stated and would otherwise be the fix itself, but as shipped nothing runs.

R400.note: The options passed (dtdload:false, dtdvalid:false, noent:false) are already libxmljs' defaults - every parser flag is off unless set truthy - so the parser flags reaching xmlReadMemory are unchanged and the write-up's claim that defaults enable entity substitution is wrong; a fix that changes anything would add nonet:true and/or reject a DOCTYPE before parsing; no observable behaviour changes.

R401.note: Extension allowlist (.png/.jpg/.jpeg, lower-cased) plus a secrets.token_hex name closes both the dangerous-extension write and the traversal via file.filename; the returned path now carries the generated name, which the write-up states, and the only newly rejected inputs are images with an extension outside the png/jpeg set, which is the CWE-434 restriction itself rather than an extra one.

R402.note: Gate::allows() replaced with Gate::authorize(), which throws AuthorizationException (403) before the save; authorised callers see the identical JSON response.

R403.note: Rejecting uri.getHost() != null stops http://evil.com and //evil.com, but an opaque URI such as https:evil.com parses with host null (confirmed with java.net.URI under OpenJDK 26 in a scratch dir) and is absolute, so sendRedirect emits it verbatim as Location and a browser on a page of a different scheme resolves it to https://evil.com; the check should also reject uri.isAbsolute()/uri.getScheme() != null and require a path starting with a single '/'; the stated relative-only restriction still admits the case's own 'foo' caller and the existing error-write pattern is reused.
